source_text.body:
Create an AWS account with a coding agent
The author had Claude Code set up their AWS account, aiming to smooth the onboarding that newcomers usually struggle with.
·
Nov 24, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
The author pasted one prompt from AWS's getting-started guide into Claude Code, starting with no account. The agent asked four setup questions and ran a remote sign-up command. The author opened the URL on their own device, signed in, and pasted the code back. The agent then verified credentials, installed the Agent Toolkit and its MCP server, and deployed a small game.
How it went
Setup finished with no access keys, 25 default skills installed, and a game deployed on S3 and CloudFront. The project's Region came out different from the one the author had set, so the agent had to correct the profile.
Worth knowing
Check your project's Region in AWS settings after sign-up, because AWS assigns it. The project account also has fewer services and coarser permissions, and it isn't suited to regulated workloads.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Walk me through creating and securing a new AWS account for [my purpose, e.g. a side project]. Use the AWS CLI where you can, and give me exact steps for anything I must do in the browser, like identity verification or payment details. Finish when I have a non-root admin user with MFA, a budget alert set at [amount], and the CLI working with a test command. Pause and show me before running any command that creates billable resources or changes billing settings.
Original source: https://dev.to/aws/i-let-claude-code-create-my-aws-account-12gb
